name: TPA6132A2RTER
title: Stereo DirectPath headphone amplifier, 25 mW per channel, click and pop suppressed
summary: A stereo headphone driver whose outputs sit at 0 V, so the headphones connect without dc-blocking capacitors; an on-chip charge pump makes the negative rail for the output stage. The inputs are differential or single-ended, with the gain-setting resistors inside and four gains (-6, 0, 3 and 6 dB) picked by two pins. It runs from 2.3 V to 5.5 V on about 2.1 mA, gives 25 mW per channel into 16 Ω with the same maximum power across that supply range, and has click-and-pop suppression, output short-circuit and thermal protection, and a shutdown that draws under 1 µA.
key_figures: 25 mW typ per channel, 16 Ω, 1% THD, 1 kHz
-100 dB at 217 Hz, -90 dB at 10 kHz

pins.name: INL-
pins.function: Left channel inverting input with a differential source; the left input itself with a single-ended source.

pins.name: INL+
pins.function: Left channel non-inverting input with a differential source; tied to ground for a single-ended source.

pins.name: INR+
pins.function: Right channel non-inverting input with a differential source; tied to ground for a single-ended source.

pins.name: INR-
pins.function: Right channel inverting input with a differential source; the right input itself with a single-ended source.

pins.name: OUTR
pins.function: Right channel headphone output, wired to the right contact of the headphone jack.

pins.name: HPVSS
pins.function: Charge pump output: the negative supply of the output amplifiers. Takes a 1 µF capacitor to ground.

pins.name: CPN
pins.function: Flying capacitor, negative end: one side of the 1 µF capacitor that sits between CPP and CPN.

pins.name: CPP
pins.function: Flying capacitor, positive end: the other side of the 1 µF capacitor between CPP and CPN.

pins.name: HPVDD
pins.function: Positive supply of the headphone amplifiers, made inside the chip. Takes a 2.2 µF capacitor; never joined to VDD.

pins.name: EN
pins.function: Enable. Logic low shuts the amplifier down; logic high turns it on.

pins.name: SGND
pins.function: Amplifier reference, wired to the ground contact of the headphone jack.

pins.name: OUTL
pins.function: Left channel headphone output, wired to the left contact of the headphone jack.

pins.name: Thermal Pad
pins.function: Exposed pad underneath; solder it to a land on the board, and either ground that land or leave it unconnected.

notes: The I/O/P column misprints INR- as O, OUTR as I, G1 as P, EN as P, SGND as O and OUTL as P.

circuits.title: Typical application with differential inputs
circuits.description: Both channels take a differential source, each of the four inputs through its own series coupling capacitor, and drive a stereo headphone jack straight from OUTL and OUTR with no output capacitors. SGND and PGND both go to ground. VDD runs from the battery with 2.2 µF to ground; HPVDD has its own 2.2 µF; a 1 µF flying capacitor joins CPP and CPN and HPVSS has 1 µF to ground. EN, G0 and G1 come in as logic lines.
notes: Equation 4 sets CIN; at 6 dB gain and a 20 Hz corner it gives at least 0.6 µF, and 0.68 µF is the value chosen.

circuits.title: Typical application with single-ended inputs
circuits.description: Each channel takes a single-ended source through a 1 µF coupling capacitor into its inverting input, with the non-inverting input tied to ground. The outputs drive a stereo headphone jack directly, and the jack sleeve and both SGND and PGND go to ground. The supply, HPVDD, flying and HPVSS capacitors are the same as with differential inputs: 2.2 µF, 2.2 µF, 1 µF and 1 µF.

circuits.title: Simplified schematic with a codec source
circuits.description: A codec's differential stereo outputs feed the four inputs through series coupling capacitors; the outputs drive a stereo jack whose sleeve is grounded. VDD comes from the battery, EN, G0 and G1 are logic lines, and HPVDD, the flying capacitor and HPVSS each carry a capacitor.

operation.text: A single-supply headphone amplifier normally sits at half supply and needs large series output capacitors, which form a high-pass filter with the 16 Ω to 32 Ω headphone, cost board area and height, and cause a pop as they charge and discharge. A capless amplifier instead drives the jack sleeve with a bias voltage, so the sleeve must not be grounded and only floating-ground headphones work. The TPA6132A2 makes a negative rail with its charge pump and swings its outputs both ways around 0 V, so the jack sleeve is grounded and other accessories can share the jack.

Built-in click-and-pop circuitry lets the amplifier start and stop without output transients; the outputs stay at 0 V dc while powered. Start-up from shutdown takes 5 ms typ. Input coupling capacitors keep turn-on pop inaudible. Turn the amplifier on after the audio sources are up and settled, and off before they are turned off.

EN at 0.6 V or less shuts the device down; 1.3 V or more turns it on. In shutdown the supply current is under 1 µA (0.7 µA typ), each input looks like 10 kΩ, the outputs look like 20 Ω, and input-to-output attenuation is 80 dB.

Two pins set the gain with internal resistors: G0 and G1 both low gives -6 dB, G0 high alone 0 dB, G1 high alone 3 dB, both high 6 dB (low is 0.5 V or less, high 1.3 V or more). The amplifier inverts: the gain is OUT over IN-. The input resistance per pin falls from 26.4 kΩ at -6 dB to 13.2 kΩ at 6 dB.

The differential input structure gives high rejection of supply and RF noise, which matters where RF bursts modulate the supply in the audio band, for example the 217 Hz frame rate of GSM phones. AC supply rejection is -100 dB at 217 Hz and -90 dB at 10 kHz.

The maximum output power stays the same from 2.3 V to 5.5 V supply instead of rising with the supply, which makes limiting the loudness reaching the listener (acoustic shock) easier and lets the signal be set for the lowest supply.

The coupling capacitors block source dc and keep the full dynamic range, and with the internal input resistor they form a high-pass filter whose corner moves with gain. They may be omitted if a differential drive below ±1 V feeds the inputs and its common-mode level stays inside the -0.5 V to 1.5 V input range, but turn-on pop may then get worse and should be checked in the system. Use X5R or better.

The flying capacitor sits between CPP and CPN; the HPVSS capacitor must be at least as large as the flying capacitor for full charge transfer. Both are low-ESR ceramics, X5R or better, typically 1 µF to 2.2 µF. Values down to 0.47 µF can be used, at the cost of higher THD. The charge pump switches at 1275 kHz typ.

Decouple VDD with a 2.2 µF low-ESR ceramic (X5R or better) within 5 mm of the pin, 0402 or smaller where possible; a further 10 µF or more helps filter low-frequency supply noise but is seldom needed. HPVDD connects only to a 2.2 µF ceramic to ground, also within 5 mm, which keeps the internal bias supply stable. HPVDD is generated inside: tying it to VDD or any outside supply can damage the device. Give each capacitor ground a short return to the chip; poor decoupling degrades audio and EMC.

SGND is the reference input and goes to the ground pin of the headphone connector; this keeps turn-on silent and the offset low. Do not put more than ±0.3 V on SGND. PGND is the power ground, and the VDD, HPVDD and HPVSS capacitors return to it.

Solder the exposed pad to a board land: the joint is needed for mechanical strength and helps heat flow. The land is either grounded, on the same ground as PGND (pin 10), or left floating; never connect it to VDD or another supply. The board layout concept routes the differential input pairs as matched traces, brings the enable line in at the top edge beside the battery feed and the gain lines at the bottom, and places the two 2.2 µF capacitors next to pins 12 and 14 and the two 1 µF capacitors next to pins 8, 9 and 11.

The outputs are protected against short circuit and thermal overload; thermal shutdown trips at 150 °C with 20 °C hysteresis. OUTL and OUTR withstand ±8 kV HBM, which eases meeting IEC 61000-4-2 in the end product.
